title: cure_cost_v1
description: What it costs to clear or replace one element, at market. Asked of the record rather than declared in a table, because a synchronisation fee is a real, quotable, researchable number and a hand written constant is a guess wearing a currency symbol. Returns a range with its basis, so a producer can see what the figure rests on.

rate_found.description: Whether the public record supports a rate at all. False is a real answer and must not be rendered as zero.

rate_unit.description: What the figure is priced against. A per second archive rate and a flat synchronisation fee are not comparable and must not be summed as though they were.

scope.description: The rights scope the figure covers: media, territory and term. A festival licence and a worldwide perpetual buyout differ by an order of magnitude for the same cue.

basis.description: What the range actually rests on: a published rate card, a trade report, a guild schedule, or an inference from comparable deals. This is the field that decides whether the number may be shown to a producer.

confidence_note.description: Why this range is wide or narrow. Licensing is negotiated and most deals are confidential, so a wide range is often the honest answer.

obtainable.description: Whether the right can be licensed at any price. Some cannot: an estate that refuses, a mark holder who does not license to productions. Unobtainable is a different finding from expensive.
